result.rationale: The diff adds an unconditional token-refresh fetch plus prisma.credential.update before every `return new jsforce.Connection(...)` in salesforce/lib/CalendarService.ts, with no expiry check — confirmed verbatim in the diff. The guard `if (response.statusText !== "OK") throw new HttpError({ statusCode: 400 ...})` is indeed fragile because fetch's statusText is empty on HTTP/2, turning successful refreshes into a thrown error. Both the hot-path regression and the statusText defect are directly visible in the added lines.

judged_text: The new refresh fetch runs unconditionally before every jsforce connection creation (not gated on token expiry), and its success check `response.statusText !== "OK"` breaks under HTTP/2 where statusText is an empty string. Every Salesforce calendar operation now pays an extra token-refresh HTTP round trip plus a prisma.credential.update even when the stored token is still valid (hot-path regression on a path previously served with zero extra calls), and on any HTTP/2 response the statusText check throws HttpError 400 even for a successful refresh, disabling Salesforce sync entirely on such connections.
